logline: A Seoul dentist opens a clinic in a seaside village and clashes with the town's beloved jack-of-all-trades handyman.

renewal.note: Completed 16-episode run in October 2021. No sequel.

bollymeter.basis: Variety's sixth-best international show of 2021; finale hit 12.67% cable ratings; craft ceiling is the leisurely pace, which divides viewers cleanly.

pull_quotes.text: The story's simplicity and lightheartedness has a refreshing vibe amid the doom and gloom of the pandemic.

seasons.review_body: Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha worked precisely because it refused ambition. Variety placed it sixth on its best international TV of 2021 list, NME ranked it eighth in its K-drama year-end, and the finale drew a 12.67% nationwide cable rating. The MyDramaList audience gave it 8.7 across 110,000 users. Critics split on pace: the warmth camp, including Variety and NME, cited the seaside setting and Shin Min-a and Kim Seon-ho's chemistry as sufficient reasons to stay sixteen episodes. Decider and a smaller dissenting cohort noted the pacing as genuinely slow rather than deliberately leisurely, and flagged a second-half tonal shift toward heavier melodrama. The show's Netflix India performance mirrored its domestic one: consistent viewership from an audience self-selecting for comfort.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A sharp-tongued Seoul dentist arrives in the sleepy coastal town of Gongjin after losing her job, and immediately clashes with Du-sik, the village's unofficial handyman who seems to be everyone's person except hers. The seaside atmosphere and comic sparring are fully operational from the first scene.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Du-sik fixing something that was not technically broken, then charging nothing and leaving before Hye-jin can say thank you - the first hint that the show is not going to follow the rules it seems to be setting up.

critic_note.text: The story's simplicity and lightheartedness has a refreshing vibe amid the doom and gloom of the pandemic.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 7
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The midpoint is where Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha stops being purely comic and shows what is underneath Du-sik's relentless helpfulness. The show earns its tonal shift by spending six episodes building the warmth it now risks cooling.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A first piece of Du-sik's backstory delivered not through exposition but through a detail only Hye-jin notices.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 11
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A typhoon episode that the show uses to compress its emotional timeline: danger, community, and a confession that the comfortable pace of the season had been deferring. The earlier slow pacing complaints find their strongest counterpoint here, as the episode reframes patience into momentum.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment when the village acts as a single organism in the storm - the show's case for why community drama is worth sixteen episodes.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale drew 12.67% nationwide, the show's highest rating. It closes the Hye-jin and Du-sik arc without sentimentality, trusting the audience to fill in the gaps rather than walking through every resolution explicitly - the formal confidence of a show that knows exactly what it is.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The last scene on the beach - the show's final image earns the entire season's investment in its setting.

critic_note.text: Kept things simple; never in danger of alienating its committed audience, which was hooked to the last.
